title: Every question needs a way to answer
statement: Never ask a question or invite a response, on screen or aloud, without a way for the learner to give it, including a lesson's closing question.
detail: Internal reviews of a grade 3 reading course found a lesson ending on a question with no way to take input, which looked incomplete, and a guide line asking the child to tell a story when nothing was listening. The rule now gives every question on screen an input, and every authored lesson closes on a receipt that states what the child did and asks nothing (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/rules/ui.md`, lines 210-225). The general case, a question anywhere with no input beside it, is not yet checked.

evidence.quote: Every question on screen has an input. A closing prompt with no way to respond is not a closing.
it also says “Now tell a story about a time when you did something clever.” but we are not listening so should probably remove it, happened in issue 6 as well
What is not checked is the general case, a question node anywhere with no input beside it.
**Rule.** Every question on screen has an input. A closing prompt with no way to respond is not a closing.
Course ending with a question which has no way to take input looks incomplete.
every authored lesson closes on a `receipt`, which states what the child did, the words they learned and what they now understand, and asks nothing.
What is not checked is the general case, a question node anywhere with no input beside it.
